topic: التعويض عن القرار غير المشروع — زاوية جديدة: 3 علامات تحذيرية قبل اتخاذ القرار
prompt: A medium‑shot, eye‑level view of a modern small‑business office that opens onto a construction site. In the foreground, a mid‑30s entrepreneur in a plain button‑down shirt and jeans sits at a wooden desk. He leans slightly forward, his right hand holding a thick, white‑paper administrative decision that bears a faint official seal in the corner; a bold red “CANCELLED” stamp overlays the lower edge. His left hand rests on a second, older document of the same size, stamped “APPROVED” in green, with a faint signature visible. Between the two papers lies a bright‑yellow highlighter marking a paragraph, and a red pen circles a line on the cancelled decision. Spread across the desk are a laptop displaying a spreadsheet of project costs, a coffee mug, and a small scale model of the development—a partially built office tower with scaffolding and a crane miniature perched on the roof. A ruler and a calculator sit nearby, suggesting a detailed review of figures. Through a large glass window behind the desk, the half‑finished construction site is visible: the skeletal steel frame of the tower, a crane with its hook lowered, and a “STOP WORK” orange safety sign taped to a nearby beam. Piles of raw materials—steel beams, concrete bags—are stacked but untouched, indicating halted progress. The daylight is bright, casting crisp shadows that emphasize the unfinished structure, while the interior is lit by soft, diffused natural light spilling onto the desk. The composition places the two contrasting decisions front and center on the desk, the cancelled one slightly angled toward the viewer to draw focus, while the halted construction visible through the window provides the concrete evidence of direct, tangible loss. The overall mood is one of careful assessment, with the entrepreneur scrutinizing the paperwork before deciding on any further action.
